title: Tasneem Kazmi v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
coram: Rajan Roy, J.; Om Prakash Shukla, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; process 4.4 indemnity bond if submitted.
headnote: A tenant claiming possession is entitled only to have a separate-connection application processed under clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 if an indemnity bond is submitted and tenancy and possession are inquired into; the order confers no title or possession.
facts: The petitioner sought a writ for a separate electricity connection from Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited. She claimed to be a tenant in possession of the premises; rent-tribunal proceedings were pending. Counsel relied on a 21 January 2025 order in another flat-owner case, Mohd. Nooruz Zaman, and on Seema Mansoor and Chandu Khamaru. The licensee's counsel submitted that the petitioner had not furnished an indemnity bond. Notice to opposite parties 5 to 7 was dispensed with.

holding_units.holding: Subject to inquiry into the petitioner's tenancy and possession, if an indemnity bond is submitted the licensee shall process it for grant of a separate electricity connection as per the Supply Code, especially clause 4.4, within four weeks. The order confers no right of possession or title and does not prejudice opposite parties 5 to 7.

not_decided.note: The order confers no right of possession or title and does not prejudice opposite parties 5 to 7 in pending or future proceedings concerning the premises.
